t.4.45.1: When the lords of the vānaras had gone, Rāma said to Sugrīva: "How is it that you know the entire circle of the earth?"
t.4.45.3: When Vālī was chasing the Dānava named Dundubhi, who had the form of a buffalo, toward the Malaya mountain,
t.4.45.2: Then Sugrīva, self-possessed and bowing humbly, said to Rāma: “Let it be heard; I shall relate everything in detail, O bull among men.”
t.4.45.4: Then the buffalo entered a cave of Malaya, and Vālī too entered Malaya there, wishing to kill him.
t.4.45.5: Then I was stationed there, away from the cave, like one held in check by water; and Vālī did not come out, even when a year had passed.
t.4.45.6: Then the cave was filled with a gushing torrent of blood. Seeing that, I was astonished and tormented by the poison of grief for my brother.
t.4.45.7: Then, convinced that my elder had clearly been slain, I placed a rock as large as a mountain at the mouth of the cave, thinking, 'Unable to come out, the buffalo will perish.'
t.4.45.9: Then Vālī returned, having slain that bull among Dānavas; and so I gave back the kingdom, out of reverence and constrained by fear.
t.4.45.8: Then, despairing of his life, I came to Kiṣkindhā, and the great kingdom was won, and Tārā together with Rumā; and there I was living with my friends, free from all distress.
t.4.45.10: That evil-minded Vālī, his senses deeply agitated and eager to kill me, chased me out of anger as I fled with my ministers.
t.4.45.11: Then I, together with my companions, was chased by that Vālin, and as I fled I saw various rivers, forests and cities.
t.4.45.12: Then indeed the earth was seen by me looking like the surface of a mirror, like a whirling firebrand, and as small as a cow's hoofprint.
t.4.45.13: Then, going first to the east, I took refuge in the southern quarter, and again, stricken with fear, I went to the western quarter; but as I was going toward the northern quarter, Hanumān then spoke to me.
t.4.45.14: Now I remember, O king, how Vālī, lord of the monkeys, was at that time cursed by Mataṃga in this very circle of hermitages.
t.4.45.15: Should Vālī ever enter it, his head would burst into a hundred pieces. There our dwelling will be happy and free from anxiety.
t.4.45.17: Thus, O king, the entire circle of the earth was then observed by me with my own eyes; after that I came to the cave.
t.4.45.16: Then, O son of a king, having reached the mountain Ṛśyamūka, Vālī did not enter it at that time, out of fear of Mataṃga.
